title: OYM Trilogy 2026 Leg 2 Review: Ayala Triangle Series Race in Makati's Financial District
seo_title: OYM Trilogy 2026 Leg 2 Review | Makati Philippines Race
meta_description: OYM Trilogy 2026 Leg 2: September 27 at Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati. A multi-distance series leg (21K, 16K, 10K, 5K) from OYM — registration pending.
dek: Set for 27 September 2026 at Ayala Triangle Gardens in Makati — the Philippines' premier financial district — this OYM Trilogy Leg 2 offers four distances including an unusual 16K mid-distance. Registration is pending.
verdict: OYM Trilogy 2026 Leg 2 brings the distinctive multi-leg running series back to Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati's signature urban park in the heart of the Philippines' financial district. Four distances — 21.1K, 16K, 10K, and 5K — give runners a genuine range, and the 16K middle distance is an uncommon stepping-stone option that sits between the standard 10K and half marathon, reflecting a race organiser that understands runners want more than a binary choice. The series format — with cumulative points or standings across multiple legs — adds competitive structure that a standalone one-off race cannot offer, appealing to runners who treat the calendar as a season rather than a collection of isolated events. Ayala Triangle is one of Metro Manila's most attractive race venues: a landscaped green space ringed by high-rise offices, jogging paths, and restaurants, with the Makati skyline providing a uniquely urban backdrop that no suburban car park or convention-centre race can match. September in Metro Manila falls at the tail of the southwest monsoon, meaning the probability of rain is declining but not zero, and humidity remains high enough to affect pacing for the longer distances. Registration has not yet been announced as of early August 2026, which is the primary obstacle to committing. For Metro Manila runners who value a series format, a genuinely attractive urban-park venue, and a distance spread that goes beyond the standard 5K/10K/21K template, the OYM Trilogy Leg 2 is worth tracking closely. Mark 27 September 2026 and monitor OYM channels for registration announcements.

sections.heading: Ayala Triangle Gardens: Makati's Green Heart
paragraphs: Ayala Triangle Gardens is not just any race venue — it is the green centrepiece of the Makati Central Business District, a 2-hectare landscaped park surrounded by the headquarters of Philippine banking, the Makati Stock Exchange, and some of the most expensive real estate in the country [2]. On a Sunday morning in September, with the office towers quiet and the jogging paths cleared of the weekday lunchtime crowd, it transforms into one of Metro Manila's most atmospheric start/finish precincts — a pocket of greenery framed by glass and steel, with mature trees providing genuine shade at the assembly area.

The practical advantages are hard to beat: Ayala Triangle is walking distance from multiple MRT and bus stops, surrounded by parking structures, and ringed by every restaurant chain and coffee shop in the Makati ecosystem. Pre-race coffee at a proper cafe, post-race brunch within a five-minute stroll, and a race village on actual grass rather than asphalt — these are small things that add up to a materially better race-morning experience than the convention-centre or mall-parking-lot norm. For runners new to the Philippine racing scene, Ayala Triangle is about as accessible and comfortable a venue as exists in the country.

sections.heading: The OYM Trilogy Format: A Season, Not a Single Race
paragraphs: OYM has built its brand around the trilogy concept — multiple race legs spread across the calendar, with runners accumulating points or tracking their progression across the series. Leg 2, set for late September, sits in the middle of the trilogy, which typically means the field has shaken out from the Leg 1 newcomers and the competitive dynamics are becoming clear [1]. For runners who treat racing as a season-long pursuit rather than a collection of isolated events, the trilogy structure provides narrative continuity: you are not just running a half marathon, you are running your second leg of the OYM Trilogy, with a third leg still to come.

The series format also tends to breed a more familiar, community-oriented atmosphere than standalone races, because a significant portion of the field will have raced together at Leg 1. Aid-station volunteers recognise returning runners, pace groups coalesce around shared series goals, and the finish-line reunions have the warmth of a recurring social gathering rather than the transactional energy of a one-off event. For runners who value community over production scale, this is a genuine differentiator.

sections.heading: The 16K Distance: A Genuinely Useful Middle Ground
paragraphs: The 16K distance is one of the quiet signatures of the OYM Trilogy. It is not a distance that appears on many Philippine race registration forms — the industry standard is 5K/10K/21K, occasionally with a 3K thrown in for families — and its presence here signals an organiser that has thought about the runner progression pathway. Sixteen kilometres is roughly 60 percent of a half marathon: long enough to require pacing discipline and a hydration strategy, but short enough that a runner who has comfortably completed a 10K can target it as a stretch goal without the full training commitment of a 21K buildup.

For the experienced half-marathoner, a 16K can serve as a tune-up race — harder than a tempo run, less taxing than a full half, and useful as a fitness checkpoint mid-training block. For the 10K regular looking to step up, it is the bridge distance that the standard calendar so often lacks. That OYM includes it alongside the 21K, 10K, and 5K says something about the organiser's understanding of how runners actually progress through distances, rather than simply ticking boxes on a generic event checklist.

sections.heading: September in Makati: The Monsoon's Tail End
paragraphs: The race date — 27 September — sits at the tail of the Philippines' southwest monsoon season (habagat), which runs from June through September and brings the bulk of Metro Manila's annual rainfall [3]. By late September, the monsoon is typically weakening as the northeast monsoon (amihan) begins its gradual transition, but the word 'typically' does a lot of work in Manila: a late-season typhoon or a lingering tropical depression can still deliver a wet race morning.

Temperature-wise, expect a start-line reading of 25–27°C in the pre-dawn hours, climbing toward 30–32°C by mid-morning — standard tropical figures that demand hydration discipline for anyone running the 16K or 21K distances. Humidity in Metro Manila in September averages 80–85 percent, which is materially higher than what runners from temperate climates are accustomed to and will slow pace by a noticeable margin. The 5K and 10K fields get the best of the conditions; the 16K and 21K runners will be finishing as the sun climbs, so early pacing restraint pays dividends.

sections.heading: Should You Run OYM Trilogy Leg 2?
paragraphs: If you are a Metro Manila runner who values a series format over a standalone one-off, an urban-park venue over a mall parking lot, and a distance spread that includes the genuinely useful 16K middle option, the OYM Trilogy Leg 2 is one of the stronger entries on the late-September calendar. Ayala Triangle Gardens provides a race-hub experience — shade, grass, coffee within walking distance, public-transport access — that most Philippine race venues cannot match, and the trilogy structure gives the morning a competitive through-line that a single race cannot offer [1].

The primary obstacle is registration, which has not yet been announced as of early August 2026. For a late-September race, that leaves a relatively narrow window between registration opening and race day, and anyone travelling from outside Metro Manila will need to make lodging decisions before knowing whether they have a bib. The weather is a secondary variable — late September can be wet or dry, and runners should prepare for both possibilities. For those willing to track OYM's registration announcements and accept the late-monsoon humidity as part of the deal, mark 27 September 2026 at Ayala Triangle Gardens. This is a series race with genuine character in a venue that rewards the early-morning effort.
